planting.note: Set bulbs 2-3 inches deep in well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; clumps bulk up fast and reward being left undisturbed for years.

directions: 'Aquarius' is a vigorous rain lily hybrid, believed to descend from a cross between Zephyranthes candida and Z. citrina, selected by the late bulb collector E.L. Brasol for its heavy flower production. Dense clumps of narrow, grassy foliage stay low and tidy through most of the year, then send up large creamy-white, cup-shaped blooms with bright yellow anthers within days of a soaking summer rain. It repeats this bloom cycle from summer into early fall, tolerating both sun and considerable shade better than many rain lily selections. Clumps increase rapidly by bulb offsets and make a dependable, nearly maintenance-free edging or rock garden subject in warm climates.

planting.note: Plant bulbs 2-3 inches deep in well-drained garden soil in full sun; a parent of the well-known hybrid 'Prairie Sunset.'

directions: 'Capricorn' is a named rain lily selection prized for its unusual coral-apricot, star-shaped flowers, a color distinct from the more common pink, white, or yellow forms seen in the genus. It has long circulated among Gulf Coast bulb growers and garden club plant sales, and is notable as one of the parents of the popular hybrid 'Prairie Sunset,' crossed with Zephyranthes candida. Narrow, grass-like leaves stay compact through the growing season, with flower stalks emerging two to three days after a soaking rain or deep watering from late spring through fall. Established clumps multiply steadily by bulb offsets and perform best in a sunny bed or border left undisturbed for several seasons.
